original_question: For the three-machine flow-shop makespan problem F3||C_max, is the problem fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by p_max, the maximum processing time?
target_in_paper: Section 5.1, Open Problem 11: "Is F3||C_max fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the maximum processing time p_max?"
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open problem almost verbatim: it has the correct problem class F3||C_max, the correct parameter p_max, and the correct parameterized-complexity question (fixed-parameter tractability).
missing_details: F3 means a flow shop with exactly three machines; every job has one operation on each machine, and all jobs must visit the machines in the same order.
In the paper's shop-scheduling notation, processing times are operation times p_ij, so p_max means max_{i,j} p_ij over all operations, not a maximum total job length.
Preemption is disallowed by default, so the question concerns the standard nonpreemptive problem F3||C_max, not the nearby no-wait variant mentioned right after Open Problem 11.
C_max should be spelled out as the makespan, i.e. the maximum completion time over all jobs.
To be fully stand-alone in parameterized-complexity language, the question should explicitly ask for an algorithm running in f(p_max) * poly(|I|) time.
The scope should stay exactly at fixed three-machine flow shop; it should not drift to F_m, to open shop/job shop, or to the different nearby question J3||C_max parameterized by p_max and n_max.
refined_question: Given a nonpreemptive three-machine flow shop instance with job set J, where each job j has exactly three operations that must be processed on machines 1, 2, 3 in this common order with processing times p_{1j}, p_{2j}, p_{3j} in N, and writing p_max := max_{i in {1,2,3}, j in J} p_{ij}, is there an algorithm running in f(p_max) * poly(|I|) time that solves F3||C_max, that is, computes a schedule of minimum makespan C_max?
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 11 in Section 5.1 (page 6), whose wording is essentially identical. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the paper's definitions of flow shop scheduling and machine-count notation from Section 2.1.1, the operation-time notation p_ij and default nonpreemption convention from Section 2.1.2, the meaning of C_max from Section 2.1.3, and the formal meaning of fixed-parameter tractable from Section 2.2. The nearby context in Section 5.1 also clarifies that the paper is asking specifically about the fixed three-machine flow-shop problem parameterized only by the maximum operation processing time p_max, and not about the no-wait variant or the distinct nearby job-shop question involving both p_max and n_max.
